CUPS · WATER

King of Cups — Meaning

Cups

  • CategoryCups
  • SymbolWater / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Court card: King (maturity, embrace)
  • UprightCalm, Consideration, Settling your feelings
  • ReversedBottling up feelings, Watching faces, Moving people with emotion

A card about facing people calmly even when your feelings sway.

King of Cups stands for "Calm, Consideration, Settling your feelings" when upright, and "Bottling up feelings, Watching faces, Moving people with emotion" when reversed. Even with anger or anxiety, you do not have to reply right away. After settling a little, choose words that are good for both you and the other person.

Reading it in a decision — In a situation where emotions run high, like apologizing, read this card as not replying in the grip of anger or anxiety, but settling a little first and choosing words that are good for both you and the other person. Reversed, explore a way to share without bottling your feelings up forever, in words that do not blame.

The decision this speaks to: When you're torn over apologizing

SYMBOLS

The symbols in the picture

The king sits holding a cup above a wavy sea. Though the surroundings sway, the king's figure is calm — the power to choose your actions while feeling your emotions.

FOR YOUR DECISION

Hints for your decision

How to read it when you are deciding

The King of Cups holds a cup calmly on a throne floating on a rough sea. It is a card representing a maturity that does not deny the waves of emotion, and judges without wavering on top of them. In a decision, it teaches that even while feeling anxiety or impatience, you can hold them and still choose calmly. Rather than trying to erase the emotion, acknowledge 'I am feeling anxious right now,' then line up your material for judgment again. The capacity to receive the feelings of the people around you also comes alive in this choice.

How to face a familiar worry

This is a reassuring card in situations with an emotional person or circumstance, where an adult judgment is asked of you. Reversed, review whether bottling up your true heart is turning your decision cold. Sharing your emotions in words is also part of a mature choice.

Questions to ask yourself before you decide

Can you name and acknowledge the emotion you are feeling right now? Even while holding the emotion, can you line up your material for judgment calmly? Do you have the room to receive the feelings of those around you? Are you bottling up your true heart too much?

"Ease of moving forward" is the strength of the tailwind behind an option if you move on it now — not a judgment of whether things will turn out well or badly.

Now that you have read the meaning, turn to the decision in front of you. Draw a card and lay your two options side by side.
